subject: cardboardRobot
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: kid in a cardboard-box robot costume.
Style: cardboard craft.
reasoning:
I'm picturing a kid-sized cardboard box robot costume, with a box torso and a helmet-style box head that has an opening so the child's face shows through, plus painted or bottle-cap eyes on the box head for extra robot detail.

Now I'm working out the skeleton proportions for a kid humanoid roughly 1.2m tall, placing hips, torso box, helmet box, and the recessed head sphere so the proportions read correctly with the costume layered on top.

I'm defining the joint hierarchy next: hips as root, a spine chain up to the chest, then neck and head joints, plus a separate jaw joint and small lower jaw piece so the mouth can articulate independently from the skull.

For arms, I'm positioning the shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints angled slightly down and outward from the body rather than a stiff T-pose, so the rest pose looks more natural.

For hands, I'm going with chunky oven-mitt shapes made from spheres rather than detailed jointed fingers—simpler capsule-shaped digits attached to the wrist to suggest fingers without a full finger-chain rig. The arms themselves I'm treating like silvery dryer-hose tubes with ribbed rings for the cardboard-and-foil aesthetic.

Now I'm defining leg joints (hip, knee, ankle) with named polyline points, planning blue sweep-radius pants tapering down the leg, and sketching foot boxes positioned at the ankle to form sneaker shapes sitting flush with the ground. I'm also thinking through how to paint the cardboard surfaces—mixing corrugated grain texture with mottled brown coloring and tape detailing to sell the costume material.

Adding more surface textures: a control panel with dials and lights on the torso front, a "ROBO" name label on the chest, and a decal on the head sphere giving the kid a visible face with eyes, mouth, and hair peeking through the helmet.

I'm also working out the decal placement for the face -- big dark eyes with highlights, a smile, rosy cheeks, freckles -- plus small sculpted details like nose, ears, and hair tufts on the sphere-based head.

Now I'm sizing the helmet so the window reveals the kid's face properly: making the helmet a 0.34 cube with a 0.22x0.2 window, building the front wall as four boxes around the cutout, and positioning the head so it sits just behind the opening with hair peeking through at the top.

I'm also adding small flaps folded outward like cardboard box lids for ears, a coiled antenna borrowed from the clockwork kit, metallic paint for the tinfoil parts, and a soft glow material for tiny LED bulbs, plus cheek blush details in the face texture.

Now I'm working out the torso box dimensions and shoulder joint placement, making sure the arm attachment points clear the body geometry with a small sleeve stub where the kid's arms emerge from the sides.

Modeling the striped arm hose over the sleeve, simplifying it to a single silver hose sweep from shoulder to wrist with ribbing detail, then adding the mitt at the end.

Since the torus's own axis won't align with the tangent direction from a frame, I'll just rotate the geometry itself so its axis points along y, then place it using the frame orientation directly. For the arm sweep, I'll pull points from the chain's centerline rather than the surface so the rings sit correctly around the arm, spacing roughly eight rings per segment at a small radius.

For the hose I'll sweep a steel-colored tube with eight sides around the chain. For legs, I'm sweeping blue pants fabric, then adding boxy cardboard shin guards wrapped in tin-foil steel color around the knee-to-ankle bone, sizing the box to roughly fit the shin and centering it at the knee joint. I still need to figure out how to reference specific joints from the chain's joint list by name for bone attachment.

Now I'm setting up the torso's front panel as a textured plane mounted slightly off the box front, sized to cover most of the chest with dials drawn into the texture, and deciding glow should apply only to small LED details rather than the whole panel. I'm also building the spine as a chain rooted at the hips joint, defining it as a polyline running upward from the hip position.

Using plain model-coordinate arrays for the at/dir params. Arms should parent off chest, legs off hips. For the clothing, I'm layering pants below the torso box starting around y 0.49, keeping the shirt hidden underneath, with thighs extending down from the hip joint—now moving on to the suspender straps.

Positioning the helmet relative to the torso box: torso top at 0.95, helmet bottom resting at 0.9, helmet center at y 1.07 with size 0.34 giving a range of 0.9 to 1.24. I'm aligning the kid's head center at 1.05 with the neck joint at 0.92 and jaw around 1.0, then working out the helmet's front window dimensions and the side wall pieces that frame it.

I realize if I make the helmet a solid box, the window hole won't actually be open since the front face would stay solid and hide the head inside — so I need to split the helmet into a back/side box plus a separate hollow front frame with real window pieces instead of one solid shape.

Now I'm adding the top flaps of the helmet box, angling two thin slanted panels outward near the top edges to mimic cardboard box flaps.

Adding a center antenna with a coiled spring, cork ball, and glowing red tip, plus cardboard-tube "ear" cylinders mounted on the helmet sides.

I'm adding more surface details: dark cylinder caps, a FRAGILE stamp, and sticker textures like "ROBO KID". I'm also wrapping a hazard-stripe tape texture around the torso bottom using a thin textured box, and planning a face decal on the spherical head part.

Building the face, hair, and ear details...

Still placing hair fringes...

Now I'm moving to the hands: mitten shapes with a scaled red sphere at the wrist joint, a thumb capsule, and a cuff, computing the hand center by following the elbow-to-wrist direction vector from the wrist position.

I'm weighing options for the fingers — simple red mitten-claws versus a more detailed palm-with-four-splayed-finger-capsules — leaning toward skipping full joint chains and just attaching finger capsules directly from the palm, spread outward from a normalized direction vector.

Still working out hand geometry...

Now for feet I'm building sneakers: white soles, red upper boxes with toe caps, and legs tucking into shoes at the ankle joint. I'm also adding cardboard-foil shin guards with gray tape strips wrapped around the top and bottom near the knee.

I'm defining the materials: mottled cardboard tones for the main and lighter cardboard layers, a polished steel look for foil parts, and a steel finish for hose segments with rings.

For the hand-drawn details, I'm sketching a control panel SVG with dials, colored lights, a wavy green screen, speaker grille lines, and "ROBO-9000" text, plus a heart sticker label and a "HELLO my name is ROBO KID" nametag to place on the chest.

Then I'm adding a yellow lightning bolt decal on the helmet sides with alpha cutout transparency, a "THIS SIDE UP / FRAGILE" back panel with arrows oriented correctly on the rear face, and starting the face viewBox with dark brown eye ovals with white highlights.

Now I'm adding freckles, an open smile with tongue, pink cheeks, and transparent skin background, plus a diagonal yellow-black hazard stripe texture. I'm tallying up the texture set -- panel, tag, bolt, back, face, hazard -- and considering adding a gauge decal on the torso and a side doodle to round out around eight textures total.

For the face decal, I'm positioning it on the skull surface and sizing it appropriately. I'm adding small glowing LED spheres (red, green, yellow) on the antenna and chest for lighting effects, and working out a small jaw piece beneath the head sphere -- sizing and positioning it so it protrudes slightly at the chin without clipping too far into the skull geometry.

I need bones for jaw too, plus budgeting many parts with helper functions and scale constants. I'm now setting up the imports for the builder utilities and clockwork/glow kits I'll use to construct the pieces.

Still writing helpers...

I'm deciding on tape colors—duct tape grey versus masking cream—and starting to lay out the torso as a cardboard box with a taped seam down the front.

Now I'm building the arm chains as bone paths from shoulder to wrist, attaching each one to the chest bone and naming the shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints along the way.

Continuing the arm path so the hose emerges from the box hole, then sweeping a tube along it and adding torus rings via the along helper for segmented detail.

Now I'm working out the wrist and hand attachment, computing direction from elbow to wrist points, adding a cuff ring, and planning a tape ring to cap the hose end.

For the hand itself I'm scaling a sphere into a palm shape with slight asymmetric dimensions, picking a yellow glove color, and widening the cuff cylinder.

Now I'm starting the leg construction, defining hip-to-knee-to-ankle points per side as a chain for building the leg bones.

Still shaping the shoe geometry...

For hips, I'll add a jeans-colored sphere scaled wide and short to cover the gap under the torso and between the legs. For the head, I'm reconsidering the ear cylinders to close them off so they don't look hollow, and I'm planning the antenna with a coiled wire sweep topped by a small glowing red ball.

Now I'm figuring out mounting details like a bottle-cap base for the antenna coil, optional corner bolts on the helmet, and flap slits on the helmet top using the lighter card color. I'm also positioning a gauge on the torso's lower chest area, working out the x-offset so it sits within the panel bounds without overlapping the central display.

Then I'm placing the hazard band and tag position relative to the torso's bottom edge, and deciding whether to add small physical bottle-cap buttons onto the panel itself. I settle on putting three glowing red cylinder buttons in a strip near the top of the torso, spaced along the x-axis with small radii so they read as indicator lights rather than crowding the main panel.

I'm also planning side details for the torso -- a BOLT-style decal plane near the arm holes, an ink stamp on the opposite side, and matching tape textures on the helmet. I work out the plane orientation and axis settings so these decals face outward correctly, confirm the back panel placement, and note that textured parts should use a white base color so the decal tint shows through properly.

Now I'm detailing the hazard band as a thin textured box, making sure its side faces display the texture correctly while keeping it simple since the front face is the main visible surface. I'm also considering small cardboard details like torso corrugation and side pocket flaps, then moving toward finalizing the module with concise SVG definitions for each panel.

Writing SVG code...

Still defining hair geometry...

Now I'm positioning the face decal with eyes on the skull, setting the kid skin tone, and finalizing rig roles for head and neck joints. I'm also defining the hose material with darker rings and placing the torso arm hole disc geometry.

Checking that the hose overlaps the disc so the rim shows around it, then adding the foil shin tape bands and antenna before finishing up the write.
